title: ACT CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OUT OF POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS

ACT CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OUT OF POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) This Act seeks to increase convenience for the public and advance postal services by contracting out some post office counter operations to designated eligible persons, thereby expanding access to service counters and promoting efficient operation of postal business.

Article 2 (Definitions) For purposes of this Act, "post office counter operations" means the following operations carried out at post offices:
1. Sale of postal stamps and related items (meaning postage stamps, instruments indicating postage, stamp booklets, envelopes needed for special handling of mail, and international reply coupons; the same meaning shall apply below), and acceptance of postal items;
2. Issuance and payment of postal money orders and acceptance of deposits and payments through postal giro accounts;
3. Post office savings and post office insurance services;
4. Such other operations as are specified by Presidential Decree.

Article 3 (Contracting Out Post Office Counter Operations)
(1) If the Minister of Science and ICT determines that it is necessary to enhance public access and increase the efficiency of postal operations, the Minister may contract out some post office counter operations to persons falling within any of the categories in paragraph (2) in accordance with this Act. Operations falling under Article 2, subparagraph 3 must, however, be contracted out under standards concerning operational capability and other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(2) The following persons may perform post office counter operations under contract from the Minister of Science and ICT: <Amended March 23, 2013; August 11, 2015; and July 26, 2017>
1. Local governments; cooperatives and their national federations established under Article 2 of the Agricultural Cooperatives Act; cooperatives and their national federations established under Article 2 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act; credit unions and the National Credit Union Federation under Article 2 of the Credit Unions Act; and corporations established under other special Acts;
2. Schools within the meaning of Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
3. Housing management businesses under Article 2 (1) 15 of the Multi-Family Housing Management Act, or self-management organizations under Article 6 (1) of the same Act;
4. Persons operating tourist accommodation businesses under Article 3 (1) 2 of the Tourism Promotion Act;
5. Persons who have registered the establishment of a large retail store under Article 8 of the Distribution Industry Development Act;
6. Other persons specified by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Making Contracts for Outsourced Operations)
(1) Before contracting out any portion of the post office counter operations to a person listed in Article 3 (2), the Minister of Science and ICT shall enter into an agreement requiring that person to provide those operations in an area designated by the Minister (hereinafter a "contract for outsourced operations"). <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(2) If two or more persons wish to perform outsourced post office counter operations in an area designated by the Minister, the Minister, before making the contract under paragraph (1), shall select the contractor under standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into account users' convenience, ability to carry out operations, and other relevant factors. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(3) In contracting with any person listed in Article 3 (2) under paragraph (1), the Minister may require a deposit as security in accordance with a Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(4) A contract for outsourced operations shall run for three years and may be renewed. If necessary, however, the renewal period may be set at any duration not exceeding three years.

Article 5 (Principles for Handling Outsourced Operations) A person who enters into a contract under Article 4 (1) (hereinafter a "contractor") shall handle the post office counter operations assigned under that contract (hereinafter "outsourced operations") fairly, promptly, and accurately.

Article 6 (Areas for Handling Outsourced Operations, etc.)
(1) The contractor shall handle outsourced operations within an area designated by the Minister of Science and ICT. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(2) The contractor shall equip its premises with the facilities and equipment specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 7 (Operating Hours for Outsourced Operations, etc.) The hours for handling outsourced operations, the receipt and disbursement of National Treasury funds and cash, and other matters needed for the handling of outsourced operations shall be determined by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 8 (Separate Accounting for Cash and Other Items) A contractor shall account for and keep cash and goods arising from the handling of outsourced operations separately from other cash and goods.

Article 9 (Persons Engaged in Outsourced Operations)
(1) "Persons engaged in outsourced operations" means the following:
1. Where the contractor is a corporation, its officers or employees who perform outsourced operations;
2. Where the contractor is an individual, the contractor or another person designated by the contractor to perform the outsourced operations.
(2) Persons under paragraph (1) shall be treated as persons engaged in the performance of public duties, but the State Public Officials Act shall not apply to them.

Article 10 (Protection of Users) Actions taken by a contractor in the course of handling outsourced operations under this Act shall be treated as actions of a post office.

Article 11 (Discounted Sale of Postal Stamps and Related Items)
(1) When selling postal stamps and related items to a contractor, the Minister of Science and ICT shall reduce their price as specified by Presidential Decree. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>
(2) The Minister shall pay the contractor a commission commensurate with the volume of outsourced operations handled, in accordance with an Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 12 (Provision of Government Supplies, etc.) When the Minister of Science and ICT considers it necessary for the smooth performance of outsourced operations, the Minister may supply the contractor with government stationery or other government goods or authorize their use without charge. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 13 (Reductions and Waivers of Postage) Postage arising from the contractor's handling of outsourced operations may be reduced or waived as determined by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Application of Other Laws by Analogy) To the extent compatible with the nature of the outsourced operations, the Postal Service Act, the Postal Money Order Act, the Postal Transfer Act, the Act on Postal Savings and Insurance, and other laws and regulations governing post office counter operations shall apply correspondingly to the handling of outsourced operations.

Article 15 (Treatment as a Public Official for Penalty Provisions) When applying penalty provisions under the Criminal Act or other Acts with respect to the handling of outsourced operations, a contractor, including persons engaged in outsourced operations pursuant to Article 9 (1), shall be regarded as a public official.

Article 16 (Contractor's Duty to Compensate for Damage) If a contractor causes a loss to the National Treasury intentionally or negligently while handling outsourced operations, the contractor shall compensate for the loss.

Article 17 (Delegation of Powers) The Minister of Science and ICT may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, delegate part of the authority conferred by this Act to the head of an agency under the Minister's jurisdiction. <Amended March 23, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

ADDENDA <Act No. 10349, June 8, 2010>
(1) (Entry into force) This Act enters into force six months after the date of promulgation.
(2) (Application) The amended proviso to Article 4 (4) applies beginning with the first renewal of a contract for outsourced operations entered into after this Act takes effect.
(3) (Relation to other laws and regulations) Where, at the time this Act takes effect, another enactment refers to the former Act on Contracting Out Postal Counter Operations or any of its provisions, and this Act contains a corresponding provision, the reference shall be construed as referring to this Act or its corresponding provision.
